pages.x: In November 2013 Ukraine's president, Viktor Yanukovych, under pressure from Russia, backed out of a deal to draw closer to the European Union. Huge crowds camped through the winter on the Maidan, Kyiv's Independence Square. In February 2014 about a hundred protesters were shot dead, and Yanukovych fled to Russia.

Days later soldiers in green uniforms without badges seized Crimea. Vladimir Putin at first denied they were Russian, then admitted it. After a vote held under occupation, Russia annexed Crimea in March 2014, which most of the world has never recognised. In the eastern Donbas, separatists armed by Russia started a war.

On 17 July 2014 a Malaysia Airlines plane flying from Amsterdam to Kuala Lumpur was shot down over the Donbas. Investigators found it was hit by a missile from a Russian army launcher, and in 2022 a Dutch court convicted two Russians and a Ukrainian separatist of murder. Russia denies any part in it.

Peace deals stopped the worst of the fighting, but trench warfare went on in the Donbas for eight years. Then, before dawn on 24 February 2022, Russia invaded from the north, east and south, expecting to take Kyiv in days. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, a former comedian, stayed in the capital and filmed himself in the street at night with his ministers: we are all here, he said.

The attack on Kyiv stalled. A Russian column 60 kilometres long jammed the roads north of the city, Ukrainian soldiers with Western anti-tank weapons ambushed its tanks, and by April Russia pulled back from the north. In the towns it left behind, such as Bucha, lay the bodies of civilians who had been shot, some with their hands tied.

In the south Russia took Kherson and besieged the port of Mariupol for almost three months. A bomb hit its theatre, where hundreds of people were sheltering, though the word children had been painted in huge letters on the ground outside. The last defenders, in the tunnels of the Azovstal steelworks, surrendered in May.

In September 2022 Ukraine struck back and freed most of the Kharkiv region in a few days, and in November it retook the city of Kherson. Russia called up 300,000 more men and claimed four Ukrainian regions as its own. After that the front barely moved: a war of trenches, mines and drones, where each village cost thousands of lives.

Neither side gives its losses, but by 2025 hundreds of thousands of soldiers had been killed or wounded on each side. The UN had counted over 13,000 civilians killed, and said the real number was higher. Russian strikes on power stations left Ukrainians in the cold and dark through the winters.

It is the largest war in Europe since the Second World War. It drew Finland and Sweden into NATO, and made Zelenskyy a symbol of resistance. In 2025 President Trump pushed for peace and met Putin in Alaska, but at the end of the year the fighting went on, with Russia holding about a fifth of Ukraine.
pts: Russia invaded in full on 24 February 2022
Still being fought at the end of 2025
